chunks: Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام was asked about garments made in Basra in the manner of Yemeni patterned cloth, from silk and cotton: is it suitable for the dead to be shrouded in them?
So he said: “If the cotton is more than the silk, then there is no objection.”

key_terms.الْعَصْبِ الْيَمَانِيِّ: Yemeni patterned fabric used here as a model or style of weaving
key_terms.بِالْبَصْرَةِ: in Basra, the place where the cloths were made
key_terms.ثِيَابٍ: garments or cloths being considered for use as a shroud
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can the deceased be shrouded in a fabric mixed with silk and cotton?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding shrouding the deceased in cloth made from a mixture of silk and cotton. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام permits its use when the cotton content is greater than the silk content.
